A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with matching main sections and Appendices A–J. Their text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison; local revisions and page reflow do not create material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original SEM simulations, Demand and dSprite experiments, and Framingham survival analyses, including results in Section 7 and Appendices D–J.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and data-analysis results and reports revised synthetic comparisons in Figure 3. Its empirical contribution includes the authors' Framingham analysis alongside the separately cited RCT reference.

M1.justification: The generative causal-bridge and shared-autoencoder procedure is retained, but Tables 1–2 report architectural revisions. Demand's Z decoder is shortened; dSprite gains a treatment embedding block, deeper encoder and treatment decoder, and revised outcome/proxy layers. These are benchmark-specific changes within the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Demand, dSprite, Framingham and SEM settings. The data-generation processes, represented populations and causal-estimation tasks are retained; the added competitors do not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds NMMR-U and NMMR-V to both synthetic comparisons and Kernel Alternative Proxy to dSprite. This substantially broadens the external comparison beyond DFPV. The existing DFPV variants, CB, CB+AE and Framingham CoxPH comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix F changes the synthetic train/validation split from 90/10 to 80/20. For dSprite, AdamW with learning rate 10^-4 becomes Adam with learning rate 10^-3, and the treatment reconstruction weight changes from 0.01 to 100. Together with the revised network configurations, these materially change the reported experimental settings; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 3 updates the component-comparison evidence for replacing DFPV's estimation procedure with sampling and for adding the autoencoder to CB. The questions tested remain the same. The dimensionality sensitivity study, bridge-generalization analysis and other appendix analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: The synthetic comparisons retain boxplot reporting, and Framingham retains 95% confidence intervals and the 30-run reporting in Appendix J. No new seed information, repeated-run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures are supplied.

E6.justification: Figure 3 substantially expands the synthetic results with new comparator distributions and revises results for retained variants. For example, the sampling-based DFPV dSprite median at 5,000 observations is approximately 9 in v1 and 13 in v2. These are revised reports under changed settings, rather than a controlled performance comparison. Framingham and appendix results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3 changes the second independence condition in Assumption A3 from Z independent of W given (U,X) to independence given U. This revises a formal assumption. The principal error bound, corollary and appendix derivations and proofs are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a causal-bridge error bound, generative estimation, shared autoencoding and extension to survival outcomes. The expanded comparisons provide evidence for existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: The explanations involving proxy quality, sampling and shared statistical strength are retained, as are the CEVAE instability discussion and censoring qualifications. The stated limitations concerning assumption verification and proxy selection are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F and Tables 1–2 revise the training recipe and layer specifications, including the dSprite treatment embedding. The previously stated dSprite weight decay is no longer specified. Data-generation instructions, hardware and timing information, sampling counts and the promise to release code upon publication remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work and novelty discussion are retained. Author-name corrections, expanded names, capitalization and publication metadata updates concern the same references. The new plotted competitors receive no corresponding expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized wording, notation and bibliography corrections, including an explicit reference for eta and indexed treatment inputs in Equation 13. The final related-work paragraph moves under Section 3, but the overall narrative and section structure remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 3's synthetic panels are redrawn with additional series, expanded legends and changed colors. Table 2 is reorganized to accommodate the revised architecture blocks, and some figures and text reflow. The other appendix figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: Figure 3 reduces dependence on DFPV as the sole external synthetic baseline, providing a more informative test of the claimed comparative effectiveness. Revised architecture specifications and small editorial corrections also help. The gain is limited because the added baselines lack accompanying methodological and tuning descriptions, while changed configurations prevent clean performance comparisons across versions.
